analysis: Offline ARM Thumb disassembly of saved byte-verified readback; no new MCU read/write operation.

observations.twist_callback: 0x0800b65c..0x0800b6ca converts Twist values and calls motion control 0x080049fc; no command-age update in this callback.
observations.executor_loop: 0x0800c3e0..0x0800c402 spins executor with 5000000000 ns timeout, delays 1 tick, checks a run flag at 0x24001a5c and ros_error <= 2. Unlike generic Subscriber_twist sample, no ping-agent call in this loop.
observations.error_exit: 0x0800c41c calls zeroing/stop routine 0x080043b0, then deletes task. This does not establish a bounded stop on command or transport loss.
observations.configuration: Available configuration script exposes motor PID, car type, arm settings, ROS domain/namespace/scales, reboot, firmware request. No documented stop timeout setting located.

conclusion: No supported runtime setting found to establish bounded MCU stopping. Physical tests showed motion during 1.046 s and 2.251 s agent stalls. Do not claim absence of all possible watchdogs from partial disassembly. Independent motor cutoff or a verified controller-side timeout is required before unattended drive.
